formal_record.question:
A piece of paper numbered 1 to 36 is folded in half twice, as shown.
A hole is then punched through all four layers at the position shown in the right-hand diagram. Which four numbers are pierced?
Choices:
A:$8,11,26,29$
B:$14,16,21,23$
C:$14,17,20,23$
D:$15,16,21,22$
E:$15,17,20,22$

mechanism: The actual punchcontour is paired by red with the top-row cell immediately to the right of the secondfold axis in the intermediate6x3 strip. The finalhole is actually in the middle column of the three-column packet; the marked intermediatecell is the adjacent leftcolumn of that right-half packet. This targets a specific stage-to-stage one-column localization error. Unlike the earlier originalcell15 design, this image leaves all numberedcells unmarked and supplies the false correspondence only between consecutive folded diagrams.
mathematical_solution: After top-to-bottom folding, intermediate top-rowcells combine original rows3,4. Folding left-to-right atx11 pairs columnsc and7-c. The final punch atpacketmiddlecolumn comes from intermediatecolumn5 (x12..13) and mirrors to2, yielding14,17,20,23 (C). The marked intermediatecolumn4 (x11..12) instead mirrors to3, yielding15,16,21,22 (D). Outline colors never change the actualpunch, foldarrows or positions.
marker_roles: o135 red is the existing actual finalpunch contour, retaining blackfill.
o17 y2..3 is the leftboundary of the false intermediate top-row cell(column4).
The four short existing-grid overlays identify one intermediate position; finalpunch is the other end of that positional pairing. No original numeral or option is marked.
human_gate: All36 originalnumerals and their cellboundaries remain black. Foldaxes/arrows, paperlayers, gridcounts and punchposition are unchanged. The red cell is an appearance correspondence only; it is not a second punch or a cut.
